dossier.architecture: Pivoting telescopic scoring head adapted from prior offseason arm experience.

subsystems.intake: Deployed guided intake at the end of the arm.
subsystems.transfer: Direct note path into the launcher avoids a separate amp handoff.
subsystems.scoring: Top/bottom Vortex launcher; one-stage telescope supplies amp/trap reach.
subsystems.endgame: Spring-extended winched hooks; passive carbon-fiber reaction forks tip toward stage.
subsystems.controls: Two camera/Orange Pi pairs, note-detection Limelight, collision-triggered intake retract and preset shot fallback.

versions: Wheel placement changed after Canadian Pacific to add spin. Added trap-door servo at San Diego; later season configurations require separate audit.
dossier.analysis: The design preserves a familiar kinematic platform while changing the game-piece interface. Preset fallback and modular wiring improve the chance of remaining useful after a vision or hardware fault.
limits: Intermediate undocumented changes are not inferred; specifications and plans retain their source context.

context_documents.title: 2024-359 · A shorter telescoping arm preserves direct note handling
context_documents.body:
# 2024-359: A shorter telescoping arm preserves direct note handling

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The arm retains an A-frame/shoulder architecture and reduces the telescope to one moving stage. A guided arm-end collector sends notes directly into the top/bottom-wheel launcher; extension is used for amp and trap. Multiple pose cameras and a note-detection camera support acquisition and scoring.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly says a third stage was unnecessary for the required reach. It identifies avoiding an amp handoff as a reason for consistent amp operation.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Reducing extension stages can remove mass, cable length, backlash and maintenance points while retaining the needed task envelope. The comparison must use actual amp/trap geometry and the stage clearance rules, not maximum theoretical arm reach. Direct note handling avoids transfer errors but carries the launcher’s mass and flexible note through the arm’s motion.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Verify reachable poses and structural deflection at the actual amp/trap approach. Test note retention during fast shoulder motion and clearance under the stage without relying on perfect driver positioning.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/0QAU0Ql9xy4](https://youtu.be/0QAU0Ql9xy4)

source_reviews.title: FRC Team 359 2024 Robot Reveal
source_reviews.review_basis: Read primary team reveal post and identified its embedded video.
facts: Team thanks 2910 for design inspiration. Reveal identifies the robot as Poi Pounder XXV.
source_reviews.limitations: The post does not assign individual design features to the inspiration.

source_reviews.title: Poi Pounder XXV — Team 359 2024 Robot Reveal
source_reviews.review_basis: Visually reviewed the team video’s public storyboard at roughly one-second intervals.
facts: Shows low approach to a ground note, loaded low and raised poses, a head reaching toward a practice wall opening, and a suspended chassis by the practice Stage.
source_reviews.limitations: Edited practice montage and sampled frames. No cycle timing or event reliability implied.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers — 359 Hawaiian Kids
source_reviews.review_basis: Visually inspected sampled pit interview and demonstration frames, about five seconds apart.
facts: Wide tubular rollers and a clear guide hold an orange note below the paired wheel rows. Separate close-ups show chain and sprockets near the shoulder, nested perforated arm members, and a raised end assembly.
source_reviews.limitations: Caption request returned HTTP 429. Spoken explanations, exact reduction and sensors were not verified.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Poi Pounder XXV puts a roller-guided pickup and opposing-wheel launcher on an elevated moving assembly. That arrangement carries the ring away from the floor and up toward an elevated scoring opening without requiring a long deck-level conveyor. The reveal shows the mechanism in low pickup, angled launch and extended poses and includes a suspended Stage setup. The system must preserve control of the note while the drivebase and the arm are both changing attitude. The published interview images explain that mechanical problem well even without exact joint control settings.
source_review.piece_flow: In the reveal, the robot approaches a floor ring with the outer rollers low. The pit demonstration shows a ring held across two tubular rollers, in front of a clear guide leading toward the paired launch wheel rows. A later demonstration shows the ring closer to those wheels. This supports a short transfer within the moving assembly, with the caveat that the stills do not establish the command sequence or powered contacts. Practice frames show the same head presenting a note at a wall opening and toward the Stage. A shooter shot depends on leaving the opposed wheel nip at speed, whereas a close placement depends more on head position and retention until the outlet reaches the opening.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: An A-frame-like support rises out of a low chassis and the arm moves above a densely packaged deck. Close-ups show a wide shoulder region with chain drive elements and a perforated member moving within the arm structure. The arm-end package has its own visible side plates and pulley hardware. The Stage pose occupies a much larger envelope than normal driving. A critical interference check is the sweep of the loaded head and cable loops through the upright supports, chain and adjacent field structure.

subsystems.name: Arm-end collector and note guide
subsystems.construction: Two prominent full-width tubular rollers, clear guide surfaces and side plates; the orange ring is visible across the roller opening.
subsystems.operation: Low arm poses bring the roller opening to the carpet. The guide and rollers support the ring until the opposing wheel rows can take it.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team reveal demonstrates several uses of the head. The specific reason for avoiding a separate Amp handoff remains a prior interview lead.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Retention depends on contact continuity as the arm accelerates. A guide wide enough for acquisition must still prevent the ring from migrating into one-sided launch contact.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector rollers and guide lead into the flywheel opening on the moving head. Their relative alignment must survive head motion and impacts.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect guide mounting and roller-to-roller gap after floor contact, then test note retention with the head sweeping through its normal pitch range.
subsystems.unknowns: Driven versus passive roller assignments, compression and detection sensors.

subsystems.name: Launcher and moving arm
subsystems.construction: The top/bottom wheel rows have visibly unequal lateral wheel coverage. Nested members and shoulder sprockets are visible in the interview images.
subsystems.operation: Shoulder motion changes presentation angle. The arm also reaches farther in the practice scoring poses than in the floor pose.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team credits 2910 broadly. The claimed choice to eliminate an extension stage awaits a readable primary account.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A longer reach increases leverage on the shoulder and magnifies angular play at the outlet. Unequal wheel coverage may affect spin and lateral sensitivity, but the intended effect was not established here.
subsystems.interfaces: Shoulder transmission, sliding members and end assembly all contribute to exit position. Route the head harness for the combined angular and extension limits.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check shoulder play under load, cable strain near the nested members and contact symmetry on a centered note.
subsystems.unknowns: Actuators, reeving, travel, launch settings and whether or how wheel spin was tuned.

subsystems.name: Drivebase and Stage interface
subsystems.construction: Low rectangular base with corner module hardware, upright structure and protruding endgame hardware visible in practice.
subsystems.operation: Reveal frames around the Stage show a raised head and the base lifted off the floor during the same montage.
subsystems.team_rationale: No chain-load rationale established by the reviewed text.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A repeatable suspended pose matters because the Trap opening fixes the outlet location independently of robot coordinate zero.
subsystems.interfaces: Chain engagement and chassis reaction determine reach to the opening. A note can remain in the head while this geometry changes.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect the suspension contact and arm position after a skewed engagement before judging placement consistency.
subsystems.unknowns: Module variant, chain attachment load path and field alignment logic.

revisions: February reveal and later pit frames show low and raised states of the same general layout. No dated hardware change was verified.
transferable_principles: Evaluate retention in the moving head under acceleration, not just in a stationary handoff test.
Measure outlet pose under the real chain-supported load case.
disconfirming_conditions: If guide compliance allows the note to skew during fast articulation, the short transfer can still misfeed.
If Stage swing moves the outlet beyond the opening tolerance, static extension reach is insufficient.
remaining_gaps: Primary speech or code is still needed for extension-stage rationale, camera functions, control parameters and competition climb changes.
